page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-1 is an arm64-based virtual machine instance within the c4a server family. It features 1 dedicated vCPU paired with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The underlying ARM64 architecture operates with a dedicated CPU allocation, ensuring consistent compute resources without the performance variability associated with shared-core configurations. However, the hardware profile lacks support for advanced instruction sets such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX), Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), and hardware-accelerated cryptography flags like AES or SHA_NI. This lack of specialized instruction sets represents a tradeoff for workloads requiring heavy vector math or cryptographic acceleration.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4a-highmem-1 offers a high memory-to-vCPU density on an ARM architecture, which typically provides lower power consumption and resource overhead compared to traditional x86 architectures. This makes the instance suitable for memory-sensitive but low-compute workloads. Appropriate use cases include lightweight database caching, small-scale in-memory data stores, directory services, and simple background workers that require more memory than compute capacity.
